facts.claim: Copenhagen charges no tourist tax in 2026: a municipal tourism levy requires legal authority from Parliament, which the City Council requested in June 2024 but has not been granted; a reported 2027 hotel tax for Copenhagen and Aarhus was left out of the government's 2027 finance bill (October 2026).

sources.title: City of Copenhagen: City Council minutes, 20 June 2024, item 6 (tourism levy)
Dansk Erhverv: tourism tax left out of the 2027 finance bill (9 Oct 2026)

its own papers set out the obstacle: a tourism levy requires legal authority
For 2026, there is no tourist tax.

facts.claim: Denmark's VAT rate is generally 25% of the value of goods and services; in retail prices VAT is included and amounts to 20% of the price.

facts.claim: The M2 metro runs from Copenhagen Airport (Terminal 3) via Christianshavn, Kongens Nytorv and Nørreport; the Metro puts the airport-to-centre ride at 14 minutes, with trains about every 2 minutes in rush hour, every 3 off-peak, and from 01-07 about every 8 minutes after Fri/Sat and every 20 minutes other nights.
